import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Grünbaum's conjecture on spherical polyhedra that tile space by translation

Can every spherical non-convex polyhedron that tiles space by translation have its faces grouped
into patches with the same combinatorial structure as a parallelohedron?

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Parallelohedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/parallelohedron)
- [Gr10] Grünbaum, Branko, *The Bilinski dodecahedron and assorted parallelohedra, zonohedra,
  monohedra, isozonohedra, and otherhedra*, The Mathematical Intelligencer 32 (2010), 5–15.
  [doi:10.1007/s00283-010-9138-7](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00283-010-9138-7)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry Pointwise

namespace CanEverySphericalNonConvexPolyhedronThatTilesSpaceByTranslationHaveI

/-- A set `P ⊆ ℝ³` *tiles space by translation* if some family of translates of `P` covers `ℝ³`
and any two distinct translates in the family have disjoint interiors. -/
def TilesByTranslation (P : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set ℝ³, (⋃ t ∈ T, t +ᵥ P) = Set.univ ∧
    T.Pairwise fun s t => Disjoint (interior (s +ᵥ P)) (interior (t +ᵥ P))

/-- A (planar, not necessarily convex) *polygon* in `ℝ³`: a finite union of non-degenerate
triangles that lies in a plane (its affine span is two-dimensional) and is homeomorphic to a
closed disk. Equivalently, it is the region of a plane bounded by a simple closed polygonal
curve. -/
def IsPolygon (f : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  (∃ s : Finset (Fin 3 → ℝ³), (∀ t ∈ s, AffineIndependent ℝ t) ∧
    f = ⋃ t ∈ s, convexHull ℝ (Set.range t)) ∧
  Module.finrank ℝ (affineSpan ℝ f).direction = 2 ∧
  Nonempty (f ≃ₜ Metric.closedBall (0 : ℝ²) 1)

/-- A *spherical polyhedron*: a compact solid `solid ⊆ ℝ³` which is the closure of its interior
and whose boundary surface is homeomorphic to the $2$-sphere, together with a finite family of
`faces`. The faces are polygons with pairwise disjoint relative interiors whose union is the
boundary surface. Convexity is **not** assumed, so the faces may be non-convex polygons and
the solid may have re-entrant edges and vertices. -/
structure SphericalPolyhedron where
  /-- The solid body of the polyhedron. -/
  solid : Set ℝ³
  /-- The faces of the polyhedron. -/
  faces : Finset (Set ℝ³)
  isCompact : IsCompact solid
  closure_interior : closure (interior solid) = solid
  sphere : Nonempty (frontier solid ≃ₜ Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1)
  isPolygon : ∀ f ∈ faces, IsPolygon f
  sUnion_faces : ⋃₀ (faces : Set (Set ℝ³)) = frontier solid
  pairwise_disjoint : (faces : Set (Set ℝ³)).Pairwise fun f g =>
    Disjoint (intrinsicInterior ℝ f) (intrinsicInterior ℝ g)

/-- A grouping of the faces of `P` into *patches* (unions of connected subsets of faces):
a partition `𝒬` of the faces of `P` into nonempty blocks such that the union of the faces in each
block is connected. The patch corresponding to a block `q` is the union `⋃₀ q` of its faces. -/
structure SphericalPolyhedron.IsPatchDecomposition (P : SphericalPolyhedron)
    (𝒬 : Finset (Finset (Set ℝ³))) : Prop where
  nonempty : ∀ q ∈ 𝒬, q.Nonempty
  subset_faces : ∀ q ∈ 𝒬, q ⊆ P.faces
  existsUnique_mem : ∀ f ∈ P.faces, ∃! q, q ∈ 𝒬 ∧ f ∈ q
  isConnected : ∀ q ∈ 𝒬, IsConnected (⋃₀ (q : Set (Set ℝ³)))

/-- The patches of a grouping `𝒬` of the faces of a polyhedron, as subsets of its boundary
surface: the unions of the blocks of `𝒬`. -/
def patches (𝒬 : Finset (Finset (Set ℝ³))) : Set (Set ℝ³) :=
  (fun q : Finset (Set ℝ³) => ⋃₀ (q : Set (Set ℝ³))) '' 𝒬

/-- A *parallelohedron*: a convex polyhedron in `ℝ³` (the convex hull of a finite set, with
nonempty interior) that tiles space by translation. By the theorems of Fedorov, Minkowski,
Venkov and McMullen these are precisely the parallelepipeds, hexagonal prisms, rhombic
dodecahedra, elongated dodecahedra and truncated octahedra (up to affine equivalence), and
every such convex polyhedron also tiles space face-to-face by a lattice of translations. -/
def IsParallelohedron (Q : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  (∃ s : Finset ℝ³, Q = convexHull ℝ (s : Set ℝ³)) ∧ (interior Q).Nonempty ∧
    TilesByTranslation Q

/-- `F` is a *facet* (a two-dimensional face) of the convex polyhedron `Q`: an exposed subset
of `Q` whose affine span is a plane. -/
def IsFacet (Q F : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsExposed ℝ Q F ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (affineSpan ℝ F).direction = 2

/-- The decomposition of the surface `S ⊆ ℝ³` into the cells `𝒞` has *the same combinatorial
structure* as the decomposition of the surface `T ⊆ ℝ³` into the cells `𝒟` if there is a
homeomorphism `φ` from `S` onto `T` under which `c ↦ φ '' c` is a bijection from `𝒞` onto
`𝒟`. Such a homeomorphism carries intersections of cells to intersections of cells, so it
induces an isomorphism of the face structures (cells, edges, vertices, and their incidences).

Since the surfaces considered here are compact, a continuous injection `φ` on `S` with
`φ '' S = T` is automatically a homeomorphism from `S` onto `T`. -/
def CombinatoriallyEquivalent (S : Set ℝ³) (𝒞 : Set (Set ℝ³)) (T : Set ℝ³)
    (𝒟 : Set (Set ℝ³)) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ : ℝ³ → ℝ³, ContinuousOn φ S ∧ S.InjOn φ ∧ φ '' S = T ∧
    Set.BijOn (fun c => φ '' c) 𝒞 𝒟

@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem tilesByTranslation_univ : TilesByTranslation Set.univ :=
  ⟨{0}, by simp, Set.pairwise_singleton _ _⟩

@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem IsFacet.subset {Q F : Set ℝ³} (h : IsFacet Q F) : F ⊆ Q :=
  h.1.subset

@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem IsParallelohedron.convex {Q : Set ℝ³} (h : IsParallelohedron Q) : Convex ℝ Q := by
  obtain ⟨⟨s, rfl⟩, -, -⟩ := h
  exact convex_convexHull ℝ _

@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem IsParallelohedron.isCompact {Q : Set ℝ³} (h : IsParallelohedron Q) : IsCompact Q := by
  obtain ⟨⟨s, rfl⟩, -, -⟩ := h
  exact s.finite_toSet.isCompact_convexHull

/-- **Grünbaum's conjecture.** Can every spherical non-convex polyhedron that tiles space by
translation have its faces grouped into patches with the same combinatorial structure as a
parallelohedron?

Precisely: let $P$ be a non-convex polyhedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose boundary surface is
homeomorphic to a sphere and whose translated copies tile space. Is it always possible to
partition the faces of $P$ into patches (connected unions of faces) so that the combinatorial
structure of the patches (as pseudo-faces of the surface of $P$) is that of the faces of one of
the five Fedorov parallelohedra, i.e. so that there is a homeomorphism from the surface of $P$
onto the surface of a parallelohedron $Q$ taking the patches onto the facets of $Q$?

The conjectured answer is yes. Following the statement, only non-convex polyhedra are
considered; for a convex polyhedron $P$ the conclusion holds trivially (take $Q = P$ and
each patch a single face), so the statement is equivalent to Grünbaum's original formulation
[Gr10] for all polyhedra that are topologically spheres and tile space by translation. -/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem can_every_spherical_non_convex_polyhedron_that_tiles_space_by_translation_have_i :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ P : SphericalPolyhedron, ¬ Convex ℝ P.solid → TilesByTranslation P.solid →
        ∃ 𝒬 : Finset (Finset (Set ℝ³)), P.IsPatchDecomposition 𝒬 ∧
          ∃ Q : Set ℝ³, IsParallelohedron Q ∧
            CombinatoriallyEquivalent (frontier P.solid) (patches 𝒬)
              (frontier Q) {F | IsFacet Q F} := by
  sorry

end CanEverySphericalNonConvexPolyhedronThatTilesSpaceByTranslationHaveI

Minor remark: the note's parenthetical 'article's tiling is face-to-face by translation' applies to the article's definition of parallelohedron (which I handle via `IsParallelohedron`, equivalent by Fedorov/McMullen), whereas the conjecture sentence in the article and the statement only say the polyhedron 'tiles space by translation'; I followed the latter for the hypothesis on P.
modeling_decisions: 'Tiles space by translation' is formalized literally as: there is a set T of translation vectors whose translates of the solid cover ℝ³ and have pairwise disjoint interiors. No lattice or face-to-face requirement is imposed on the tiling of the (non-convex) polyhedron P; the Wikipedia entry and the article's sentence on Grünbaum's conjecture only say 'tile space by translation'. (The decomposition note's 'face-to-face' remark concerns the article's definition of *parallelohedron*, see below.)

The hypothesis 'non-convex' is included literally as `¬ Convex ℝ P.solid`. This is inessential: for a convex P the conclusion holds trivially (Q := P, singleton patches), so the statement is equivalent to Grünbaum's original formulation for all spherical polyhedra; the docstring records this.

A 'spherical polyhedron' is a compact solid equal to the closure of its interior whose frontier is homeomorphic to the 2-sphere `Metric.sphere (0:ℝ³) 1`, together with a finite set of faces: planar polygonal disks (finite unions of coplanar non-degenerate triangles, homeomorphic to a closed disk; convexity of faces NOT required) with pairwise disjoint relative interiors (`intrinsicInterior`) covering the frontier. The regularity condition `closure (interior solid) = solid` is needed to exclude the degenerate 'solid = surface' case, which would tile space trivially and falsify the statement.

The statement quantifies over every such face structure on the solid (coplanar adjacent faces are not forced to be merged). Any admissible face structure refines the maximal-face structure and a patch grouping of the maximal faces induces one of any refinement with the same patches, so this is equivalent to the version with maximal faces whenever the maximal planar regions are themselves polygons.

'Parallelohedron' is formalized by its definition (a convex polyhedron — convex hull of a finite set with nonempty interior — that tiles space by translation) instead of enumerating the five Fedorov types. The article's definition additionally asks the tiling to be face-to-face; by Fedorov/Minkowski/Venkov/McMullen every convex polytope tiling by translation is one of the five types and admits a face-to-face lattice tiling, so the class of sets is the same.
Facets of the convex polyhedron Q are its exposed subsets (`IsExposed ℝ Q F`) whose affine span has dimension 2.

'Same combinatorial structure' is formalized as the existence of a cellular homeomorphism: a homeomorphism from the surface of P onto the surface of Q under which c ↦ φ '' c is a bijection from the set of patches onto the set of facets of Q. This is the standard notion of isomorphism of cell decompositions of a sphere (it carries intersections of patches to intersections of facets, hence induces an isomorphism of the pseudo-face/edge/vertex incidence structure, and it forces each patch to be a disk). The homeomorphism is encoded as `ContinuousOn φ S ∧ S.InjOn φ ∧ φ '' S = T`, which is equivalent to a homeomorphism S ≃ₜ T since S = frontier of a compact set is compact and ℝ³ is Hausdorff.

A patch decomposition is a partition of the finite set of faces into nonempty blocks whose unions are (topologically) connected, matching 'unions of connected subsets of faces'. Faces meeting only at a vertex have connected union, but such a patch cannot be mapped onto a facet (a disk), so the two readings of 'connected' agree in the statement.
Ambient space is `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)` (repo notation `ℝ³`), the closed disk is `Metric.closedBall (0:ℝ²) 1`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Grünbaum's conjecture on spherical polyhedra that tile space by translation

A *parallelohedron* is a convex polyhedron whose translated copies tile $\mathbb{R}^3$. By
Fedorov's theorem there are exactly five combinatorial types: the parallelepiped, the hexagonal
prism, the rhombic dodecahedron, the elongated dodecahedron and the truncated octahedron.

Beyond these five convex shapes there are many *non-convex* polyhedra that tile space by
translation (for instance certain "indented" rhombic triacontahedra). Grünbaum conjectured that
every polyhedron that is topologically a sphere and tiles space by translation is nevertheless
"one of the five in disguise": its faces can be grouped into *patches* (connected unions of faces)
so that the combinatorial structure of the patches (patches as pseudo-faces, their common
boundaries as pseudo-edges) is that of the faces of one of the five Fedorov parallelohedra.

The list entry asks: *Can every spherical non-convex polyhedron that tiles space by translation
have its faces grouped into patches with the same combinatorial structure as a parallelohedron?*
The conjectured answer is yes.

## Formalisation choices

* A *spherical polyhedron* is a compact solid $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ with non-empty interior
  whose boundary is homeomorphic to the $2$-sphere, together with its finite family of faces:
  planar polygons (each a topological disk that is a finite union of convex polygons spanning a
  plane) that cover the boundary and pairwise meet only along their boundaries.
* $K$ *tiles space by translation* if some family of translates of $K$ covers $\mathbb{R}^3$ and
  the translates have pairwise disjoint interiors.
* "One of the five Fedorov parallelohedra" is rendered as "some convex polytope with non-empty
  interior that tiles space by translation"; by Fedorov's classification these are exactly the
  polyhedra of the five types.
* "The patches have the same combinatorial structure as the faces of $Q$" is rendered as: there
  is a homeomorphism from the boundary of $K$ to the boundary of $Q$ under which the preimage of
  every facet of $Q$ is a union of faces of $K$. These preimages are the patches; they are then
  automatically connected unions of faces, they partition the faces of $K$, and the incidence
  structure of patches, pseudo-edges and pseudo-vertices is that of the face lattice of $Q$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Parallelohedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/parallelohedron)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Gr10] Grünbaum, B., *The Bilinski dodecahedron and assorted parallelohedra, zonohedra,
  monohedra, isozonohedra, and otherhedra*, The Mathematical Intelligencer 32 (2010), 5–15.
  [doi:10.1007/s00283-010-9138-7](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00283-010-9138-7)
-/

namespace CanEverySphericalNonConvexPolyhedronThatTilesSpaceByTranslationHaveI

open scoped EuclideanGeometry Pointwise

/-- A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ **tiles space by translation** if there is a set $T$ of
translation vectors such that the translates $t + K$, $t \in T$, cover $\mathbb{R}^3$ and have
pairwise disjoint interiors. -/
def TilesByTranslation (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set ℝ³, (⋃ t ∈ T, t +ᵥ K) = Set.univ ∧ T.PairwiseDisjoint fun t ↦ interior (t +ᵥ K)

/-- A set $f \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is a **planar polygon** if it spans a plane (its affine span
has dimension $2$), it is a finite union of convex polygons (convex hulls of finite sets), and it
is homeomorphic to a closed disk. -/
def IsPlanarPolygon (f : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  Module.finrank ℝ (vectorSpan ℝ f) = 2 ∧
    (∃ S : Finset (Finset ℝ³), f = ⋃ s ∈ S, convexHull ℝ (s : Set ℝ³)) ∧
    Nonempty (f ≃ₜ Metric.closedBall (0 : ℝ²) 1)

/-- `IsSphericalPolyhedron K F` says that the compact solid $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ together
with the finite family `F` of its faces is a **spherical polyhedron**: $K$ has non-empty
interior, its boundary is homeomorphic to the $2$-sphere, and the faces are planar polygons that
cover the boundary and pairwise meet only along their boundaries (the relative interior of a
face is disjoint from every other face). Convexity is not assumed. -/
structure IsSphericalPolyhedron (K : Set ℝ³) (F : Finset (Set ℝ³)) : Prop where
  isCompact : IsCompact K
  interior_nonempty : (interior K).Nonempty
  sphere : Nonempty (frontier K ≃ₜ Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1)
  faces : ∀ f ∈ F, IsPlanarPolygon f
  cover : (⋃ f ∈ F, f) = frontier K
  disjoint : ∀ f ∈ F, ∀ g ∈ F, f ≠ g → Disjoint (intrinsicInterior ℝ f) g

/-- A **(convex) parallelohedron** is a convex polytope in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with non-empty interior
that tiles space by translation. By Fedorov's theorem these are exactly the polyhedra of the five
Fedorov types: parallelepiped, hexagonal prism, rhombic dodecahedron, elongated dodecahedron and
truncated octahedron. -/
def IsConvexParallelohedron (Q : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  (∃ V : Finset ℝ³, Q = convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ³)) ∧ (interior Q).Nonempty ∧ TilesByTranslation Q

/-- The **facets** of a convex polytope $Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$: its exposed faces of
dimension $2$. -/
def facets (Q : Set ℝ³) : Set (Set ℝ³) :=
  {G | IsExposed ℝ Q G ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (vectorSpan ℝ G) = 2}

/-- `HasPatchStructureOf K F Q` says that the faces `F` of the polyhedron $K$ can be grouped into
**patches** whose combinatorial structure is that of the faces of the convex polyhedron $Q$:
there is a homeomorphism $e$ from the boundary of $K$ to the boundary of $Q$ such that the
preimage under $e$ of every facet of $Q$ is a union of faces of $K$. The preimages of the
facets are the patches. -/
def HasPatchStructureOf (K : Set ℝ³) (F : Finset (Set ℝ³)) (Q : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ e : frontier K ≃ₜ frontier Q, ∀ G ∈ facets Q,
    ∃ S ⊆ F, (⋃ f ∈ S, f) = Subtype.val '' (e ⁻¹' (Subtype.val ⁻¹' G))

/-- **Grünbaum's conjecture.** Can every spherical non-convex polyhedron that tiles space by
translation have its faces grouped into patches with the same combinatorial structure as a
parallelohedron?

That is: for every compact solid $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ with faces `F` that is a spherical
polyhedron, is not convex and tiles space by translation, is there a convex parallelohedron $Q$
(one of the five Fedorov parallelohedra) and a homeomorphism from the boundary of $K$ to the
boundary of $Q$ under which every facet of $Q$ corresponds to a patch, i.e. a union of faces
of $K$? The conjectured answer is yes. -/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem can_every_spherical_non_convex_polyhedron_that_tiles_space_by_translation_have_i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (K : Set ℝ³) (F : Finset (Set ℝ³)), IsSphericalPolyhedron K F →
      ¬ Convex ℝ K → TilesByTranslation K →
      ∃ Q, IsConvexParallelohedron Q ∧ HasPatchStructureOf K F Q := by
  sorry

/-- The whole space tiles space by translation (with the single translate by `0`). -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem tilesByTranslation_univ : TilesByTranslation Set.univ :=
  ⟨{0}, by simp, by simp⟩

/-- The empty set does not tile space by translation. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem not_tilesByTranslation_empty : ¬ TilesByTranslation ∅ := by
  rintro ⟨T, hT, -⟩
  simp only [Set.vadd_set_empty, Set.iUnion_empty] at hT
  exact Set.empty_ne_univ hT

/-- The empty set is not a spherical polyhedron, whatever its faces. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem not_isSphericalPolyhedron_empty (F : Finset (Set ℝ³)) : ¬ IsSphericalPolyhedron ∅ F :=
  fun h ↦ by simpa using h.interior_nonempty

/-- Every face of a spherical polyhedron lies on its boundary. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem IsSphericalPolyhedron.subset_frontier {K : Set ℝ³} {F : Finset (Set ℝ³)}
    (h : IsSphericalPolyhedron K F) {f : Set ℝ³} (hf : f ∈ F) : f ⊆ frontier K :=
  h.cover ▸ Set.subset_iUnion₂ (s := fun f _ ↦ f) f hf

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Grünbaum's conjecture on spherical polyhedra that tile space by translation

A *parallelohedron* is a convex polyhedron whose translated copies tile $\mathbb{R}^3$.
By Fedorov's classification there are five combinatorial types: the parallelepiped, the
hexagonal prism, the rhombic dodecahedron, the elongated dodecahedron and the truncated
octahedron.

There are also many non-convex polyhedra that tile space by translation, for instance
rhombic triacontahedra in which some triples of faces are replaced by indentations.
Grünbaum conjectured that every polyhedron whose surface is a topological sphere and which
tiles space by translation has its faces grouped into *patches* (unions of edge-connected
sets of faces) such that the combinatorial structure of the patches is the same as the
combinatorial structure of the faces of one of the five parallelohedra.

## Formalisation choices

* A *polyhedron* is a compact subset of $\mathbb{R}^3$ that is the closure of its interior
  and whose boundary is contained in a finite union of planes. It is *spherical* if its
  boundary is homeomorphic to the $2$-sphere.
* The *faces* of a polyhedron are the closures of the connected components of the set of
  boundary points near which the boundary is a plane. These are the maximal planar pieces
  of the boundary.
* Two sets *share an edge* if their intersection contains a nondegenerate segment. A set of
  faces is *edge-connected* if it is connected under this relation.
* The *combinatorial structure* of a family of patches (or faces) is recorded by its
  adjacency graph: two patches are adjacent when they share an edge. Two families have the
  same combinatorial structure when their adjacency graphs are isomorphic. Since the face
  adjacency graphs of the five parallelohedra are $3$-connected planar graphs, this
  determines the cell structure of the patch decomposition of the sphere up to
  isomorphism (Whitney's theorem).
* "Tiles space by translation" is `tilesByTranslation` (a countable family of translates
  covering $\mathbb{R}^3$ up to a null set, with pairwise null overlaps). For compact
  polyhedra this is equivalent to an exact tiling with pairwise disjoint interiors.
* A *parallelohedron* is a convex polyhedron that tiles space by translation. By a theorem
  of Venkov and McMullen every such polyhedron also admits a face-to-face lattice tiling, so
  this agrees with the usual definition, and by Fedorov's classification the parallelohedra
  have exactly five combinatorial types.
* Convexity is not excluded. A convex polyhedron that tiles space by translation is itself
  a parallelohedron, and the grouping in which every face is its own patch works for it, so
  the convex case is trivial and the content of the conjecture lies in the non-convex case.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Parallelohedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/parallelohedron)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Gr10] Grünbaum, B., _The Bilinski dodecahedron and assorted parallelohedra, zonohedra,
  monohedra, isozonohedra, and otherhedra_. The Mathematical Intelligencer 32 (2010), 5–15.
-/

namespace CanEverySphericalNonConvexPolyhedronThatTilesSpaceByTranslationHaveI

open Topology

local notation "ℝ³" => Fin 3 → ℝ

/-- A *polyhedron* in $\mathbb{R}^3$: a compact set which is the closure of its interior and
whose boundary is contained in a finite union of planes. -/
structure IsPolyhedron (P : Set ℝ³) : Prop where
  isCompact : IsCompact P
  closure_interior : closure (interior P) = P
  frontier_subset : ∃ 𝓗 : Set (AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³), 𝓗.Finite ∧
    (∀ H ∈ 𝓗, Module.finrank ℝ H.direction = 2) ∧
    frontier P ⊆ ⋃ H ∈ 𝓗, (H : Set ℝ³)

/-- A *spherical polyhedron*: a polyhedron whose boundary surface is homeomorphic to the
$2$-sphere. -/
def IsSphericalPolyhedron (P : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsPolyhedron P ∧ Nonempty (frontier P ≃ₜ Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) 1)

/-- A *parallelohedron*: a convex polyhedron that tiles space by translation. By Fedorov's
classification these are the parallelepipeds, hexagonal prisms, rhombic dodecahedra,
elongated dodecahedra and truncated octahedra. -/
def IsParallelohedron (Q : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  Convex ℝ Q ∧ IsPolyhedron Q ∧ tilesByTranslation Q

/-- The set of *flat points* of the boundary of `P`: the boundary points `x` such that, near
`x`, the boundary of `P` coincides with a plane. -/
def flatPoints (P : Set ℝ³) : Set ℝ³ :=
  {x | x ∈ frontier P ∧ ∃ H : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³, Module.finrank ℝ H.direction = 2 ∧
    ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝 x, (y ∈ frontier P ↔ y ∈ H)}

/-- The *faces* of `P`: the closures of the connected components of the set of flat points
of the boundary of `P`, i.e. the maximal planar pieces of the boundary. -/
def faces (P : Set ℝ³) : Set (Set ℝ³) :=
  {F | ∃ x ∈ flatPoints P, F = closure (connectedComponentIn (flatPoints P) x)}

/-- Two sets `A` and `B` *share an edge* if their intersection contains a nondegenerate line
segment. -/
def SharesEdge (A B : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ x y : ℝ³, x ≠ y ∧ segment ℝ x y ⊆ A ∩ B

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem sharesEdge_comm {A B : Set ℝ³} : SharesEdge A B ↔ SharesEdge B A := by
  simp only [SharesEdge, Set.inter_comm]

/-- The *adjacency graph* of a family `A` of sets: two members are adjacent if they share an
edge. -/
def adjacencyGraph {ι : Type*} (A : ι → Set ℝ³) : SimpleGraph ι :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel fun i j => SharesEdge (A i) (A j)

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem adjacencyGraph_adj {ι : Type*} (A : ι → Set ℝ³) (i j : ι) :
    (adjacencyGraph A).Adj i j ↔ i ≠ j ∧ SharesEdge (A i) (A j) := by
  simp only [adjacencyGraph, SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj, @sharesEdge_comm (A j), or_self]

/-- A set `S` of faces is *edge-connected* if it is nonempty and connected under the relation
of sharing an edge. -/
def IsEdgeConnected (S : Set (Set ℝ³)) : Prop :=
  (adjacencyGraph fun F : S => (F : Set ℝ³)).Connected

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem isEdgeConnected_singleton (F : Set ℝ³) : IsEdgeConnected {F} := by
  refine { preconnected := fun u v => ?_, nonempty := ⟨⟨F, rfl⟩⟩ }
  rw [Subsingleton.elim u v]

/-- A *patch decomposition* of the polyhedron `P` is a partition `𝒬` of the set of faces of
`P` into edge-connected classes; the *patches* are the unions `⋃₀ S` for `S ∈ 𝒬`. -/
structure IsPatchDecomposition (P : Set ℝ³) (𝒬 : Set (Set (Set ℝ³))) : Prop where
  subset_faces : ∀ S ∈ 𝒬, S ⊆ faces P
  isEdgeConnected : ∀ S ∈ 𝒬, IsEdgeConnected S
  partition : ∀ F ∈ faces P, ∃! S, S ∈ 𝒬 ∧ F ∈ S

/-- The adjacency graph of the patches of a patch decomposition `𝒬`: two patches are adjacent
if they share an edge. -/
def patchGraph (𝒬 : Set (Set (Set ℝ³))) : SimpleGraph 𝒬 :=
  adjacencyGraph fun S : 𝒬 => ⋃₀ (S : Set (Set ℝ³))

/-- The adjacency graph of the faces of a polyhedron `Q`: two faces are adjacent if they
share an edge. -/
def faceGraph (Q : Set ℝ³) : SimpleGraph (faces Q) :=
  adjacencyGraph fun F : faces Q => (F : Set ℝ³)

/-- The trivial grouping, in which every face of `Q` is its own patch, is a patch
decomposition of `Q` whose patch graph is the face graph of `Q`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem isPatchDecomposition_singleton (Q : Set ℝ³) :
    IsPatchDecomposition Q ((fun F => {F}) '' faces Q) ∧
      Nonempty (patchGraph ((fun F => {F}) '' faces Q) ≃g faceGraph Q) := by
  have hinj : Set.InjOn (fun F : Set ℝ³ => ({F} : Set (Set ℝ³))) (faces Q) :=
    Set.singleton_injective.injOn
  refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩, ⟨?_⟩⟩
  · rintro S ⟨F, hF, rfl⟩
    simpa using hF
  · rintro S ⟨F, hF, rfl⟩
    exact isEdgeConnected_singleton F
  · intro F hF
    refine ⟨{F}, ⟨⟨F, hF, rfl⟩, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
    rintro S ⟨⟨G, hG, rfl⟩, hFS⟩
    simp_all
  · refine SimpleGraph.Iso.symm ⟨Equiv.Set.imageOfInjOn _ _ hinj, ?_⟩
    rintro ⟨F, hF⟩ ⟨G, hG⟩
    simp only [patchGraph, faceGraph, adjacencyGraph_adj, Equiv.Set.imageOfInjOn,
      Equiv.coe_fn_mk, ne_eq, Subtype.mk.injEq, Set.singleton_eq_singleton_iff,
      Set.sUnion_singleton]

/-- Sanity check: for a parallelohedron the conclusion of the conjecture holds with the
trivial grouping. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem exists_patchDecomposition_of_isParallelohedron {Q : Set ℝ³}
    (hQ : IsParallelohedron Q) :
    ∃ 𝒬 : Set (Set (Set ℝ³)), IsPatchDecomposition Q 𝒬 ∧
      ∃ Q' : Set ℝ³, IsParallelohedron Q' ∧ Nonempty (patchGraph 𝒬 ≃g faceGraph Q') :=
  ⟨_, (isPatchDecomposition_singleton Q).1, Q, hQ, (isPatchDecomposition_singleton Q).2⟩

/--
**Grünbaum's conjecture** [Gr10]. Can every spherical (non-convex) polyhedron that tiles
space by translation have its faces grouped into patches with the same combinatorial
structure as a parallelohedron?

That is: for every polyhedron $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ whose boundary is a topological
sphere and whose translated copies tile $\mathbb{R}^3$, is there a partition of the faces of
$P$ into edge-connected patches such that the adjacency graph of the patches is isomorphic
to the face adjacency graph of one of the five parallelohedra?

The conjectured answer is yes.
-/

theorem can_every_spherical_non_convex_polyhedron_that_tiles_space_by_translation_have_i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ P : Set ℝ³, IsSphericalPolyhedron P → tilesByTranslation P →
      ∃ 𝒬 : Set (Set (Set ℝ³)), IsPatchDecomposition P 𝒬 ∧
        ∃ Q : Set ℝ³, IsParallelohedron Q ∧ Nonempty (patchGraph 𝒬 ≃g faceGraph Q) := by
  sorry

  face_is_polygon : ∀ f, ∃ s : Set Vertex, s.Finite ∧
    face f = convexHull ℝ (vertex '' s)
  edge_closed : ∀ e, IsClosed (edge e)
  edge_convex : ∀ e, Convex ℝ (edge e)
  edge_dimension : ∀ e, Module.finrank ℝ (affineSpan ℝ (edge e)).direction = 1
  edge_is_segment : ∀ e, ∃ v w, v ≠ w ∧ edge e = segment ℝ (vertex v) (vertex w)
  boundary_eq : frontier carrier = ⋃ f, face f
  face_intersection : ∀ f g, f ≠ g →
    face f ∩ face g = ∅ ∨
      (∃ e, face f ∩ face g = edge e) ∨
      (∃ v, face f ∩ face g = {vertex v})
  edge_is_intersection : ∀ e, ∃ f g, f ≠ g ∧ face f ∩ face g = edge e
  vertex_on_boundary : ∀ v, ∃ f, vertex v ∈ face f

attribute [instance] Polyhedron.faceFintype Polyhedron.edgeFintype
  Polyhedron.vertexFintype

/-- The boundary of `P` is topologically a two-sphere. This is the meaning of “spherical” in
Grünbaum's conjecture. -/
def Polyhedron.IsSpherical (P : Polyhedron) : Prop :=
  Nonempty ((frontier P.carrier : Set E3) ≃ₜ (Metric.sphere (0 : E3) 1 : Set E3))

/-- Translation of a subset of Euclidean space. -/
def translate (s : Set E3) (t : E3) : Set E3 := t +ᵥ s

/-- Two translates of `P` meet face-to-face if their intersection is empty or is one and the
same translated face, edge, or vertex of both copies. -/
def Polyhedron.TranslatesMeetFaceToFace (P : Polyhedron) (t u : E3) : Prop :=
  translate P.carrier t ∩ translate P.carrier u = ∅ ∨
  (∃ f g, translate P.carrier t ∩ translate P.carrier u = translate (P.face f) t ∧
    translate (P.face f) t = translate (P.face g) u) ∨
  (∃ e d, translate P.carrier t ∩ translate P.carrier u = translate (P.edge e) t ∧
    translate (P.edge e) t = translate (P.edge d) u) ∨
  (∃ v w, translate P.carrier t ∩ translate P.carrier u = {t + P.vertex v} ∧
    ({t + P.vertex v} : Set E3) = {u + P.vertex w})

/-- The translated copies of `P` form an exact face-to-face tiling of `E3`. -/
def Polyhedron.TilesByTranslation (P : Polyhedron) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set E3, T.Countable ∧ 0 ∈ T ∧
    (⋃ t ∈ T, translate P.carrier t) = univ ∧
    (∀ ⦃t⦄, t ∈ T → ∀ ⦃u⦄, u ∈ T → t ≠ u →
      Disjoint (interior (translate P.carrier t)) (interior (translate P.carrier u))) ∧
    (∀ ⦃t⦄, t ∈ T → ∀ ⦃u⦄, u ∈ T → t ≠ u →
      P.TranslatesMeetFaceToFace t u)

/-- Adjacency of two faces along an edge. -/
def Polyhedron.FaceAdjacent (P : Polyhedron) (f g : P.Face) : Prop :=
  f ≠ g ∧ ∃ e, P.edge e ⊆ P.face f ∧ P.edge e ⊆ P.face g

/-- The patches indexed by `A` are adjacent when some face in one is adjacent to some face in the
other. A map `q : P.Face → A` represents the partition of the faces into its fibers. -/
def Polyhedron.PatchAdjacent {A : Type} (P : Polyhedron) (q : P.Face → A) (a b : A) : Prop :=
  a ≠ b ∧ ∃ f g, q f = a ∧ q g = b ∧ P.FaceAdjacent f g

/-- The closed patch formed by all faces in one fiber of `q`. -/
def Polyhedron.patch {A : Type} (P : Polyhedron) (q : P.Face → A) (a : A) : Set E3 :=
  ⋃ f, ⋃ (_ : q f = a), P.face f

/-- The fibers of `q` are nonempty connected patches and have exactly the combinatorial structure
of the faces of `Q`. Besides preserving adjacency, preservation of the nerve records which
collections of closed patches meet at pseudo-edges and pseudo-vertices. Connectedness of all
nonempty intersections prevents a pseudo-edge or pseudo-vertex from having several components. -/
def Polyhedron.PatchesModel (P Q : Polyhedron) (q : P.Face → Q.Face) : Prop :=
  Function.Surjective q ∧
  (∀ a, IsConnected (P.patch q a)) ∧
  (∀ a b, P.PatchAdjacent q a b ↔ Q.FaceAdjacent a b) ∧
  (∀ s : Set Q.Face,
    (⋂ a ∈ s, P.patch q a).Nonempty ↔ (⋂ a ∈ s, Q.face a).Nonempty) ∧
  (∀ s : Set Q.Face, s.Nonempty → (⋂ a ∈ s, P.patch q a).Nonempty →
    IsConnected (⋂ a ∈ s, P.patch q a))

/-- The displayed faces are maximal facets rather than coplanar subdivisions. For a convex
polyhedron this says that no two distinct faces lie in the same supporting plane. -/
def Polyhedron.HasMaximalFaces (P : Polyhedron) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃f g : P.Face⦄, f ≠ g → affineSpan ℝ (P.face f) ≠ affineSpan ℝ (P.face g)


/-- A three-dimensional parallelohedron: a convex polyhedron whose translated copies tile space
face-to-face. Fedorov's classification says that these have exactly five combinatorial types. -/
def Polyhedron.IsParallelohedron (P : Polyhedron) : Prop :=
  P.IsSpherical ∧ P.HasMaximalFaces ∧ Convex ℝ P.carrier ∧ P.TilesByTranslation

/--
**Grünbaum's conjecture.** Can every polyhedron in $\mathbb R^3$ whose boundary is topologically a
sphere and whose translated copies form a face-to-face tiling of space have its faces partitioned
into connected patches with the same face-adjacency (combinatorial) structure as a
parallelohedron? Convexity is not assumed; the convex instances are included, while the conjecture
is open for non-convex polyhedra.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem can_every_spherical_non_convex_polyhedron_that_tiles_space_by_translation_have_i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ P : Polyhedron, P.IsSpherical → P.TilesByTranslation →
      ∃ Q : Polyhedron, Q.IsParallelohedron ∧ ∃ q : P.Face → Q.Face, P.PatchesModel Q q := by
  sorry

end CanEverySphericalNonConvexPolyhedronThatTilesSpaceByTranslationHaveI

Modeled “tiles space by translation” as an exact countable cover by translates, with pairwise disjoint interiors and every intersection of distinct tiles equal to a common translated face, edge, vertex, or the empty set. import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Grünbaum's conjecture on non-convex polyhedra that tile space by translation

A *parallelohedron* is a convex polyhedron whose translated copies tile Euclidean $3$-space.
By Fedorov's theorem there are exactly five combinatorial types of parallelohedra: the
parallelepiped (cube), the hexagonal prism, the rhombic dodecahedron, the elongated dodecahedron
and the truncated octahedron.

There are also non-convex polyhedra that tile space by translation; these need not be
centrally symmetric. Branko Grünbaum conjectured that for every polyhedron that is
topologically a sphere and tiles space by translation, its faces can be grouped into connected
patches so that the combinatorial structure of these patches is the same as the combinatorial
structure of the faces of one of the five parallelohedra. The conjecture is open.

## Formalisation

* A (solid) *spherical polyhedron* is a compact subset of $\mathbb{R}^3$ with nonempty interior
  whose boundary is contained in finitely many planes and is homeomorphic to the $2$-sphere.
  Convexity is not assumed. (Every parallelohedron is a convex spherical polyhedron and trivially
  satisfies the conclusion of the conjecture, so the word *non-convex* in the question only
  stresses the new cases.)
* The *faces* of such a polyhedron are defined intrinsically: they are the closures of the
  connected components of the set of boundary points near which the boundary is a plane. For a
  convex polytope these are exactly its two-dimensional faces.
* *Tiling space by translation* is `tilesByTranslation`. For a compact set with nonempty interior
  whose boundary has measure zero this is equivalent to an exact tiling: some family of translates
  covers $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the translates have pairwise disjoint interiors. No face-to-face
  condition is imposed on the tiling.
* A *patch decomposition* is a partition of the set of faces into groups, each of which has a
  connected union (the *patch*).
* The patches of $P$ and the faces of $Q$ have the *same combinatorial structure* if some
  homeomorphism between the boundaries of $P$ and $Q$ maps the patches exactly onto the faces
  of $Q$. This is the natural notion of combinatorial equivalence between the cell decomposition
  of the boundary of $P$ into patches (with pseudo-edges and pseudo-vertices) and the boundary
  complex of $Q$.
* A parallelohedron is a convex spherical polyhedron that tiles space by translation. By the
  theorem of Venkov and McMullen such a polyhedron automatically admits a face-to-face lattice
  tiling, and by Fedorov's theorem it is one of the five Fedorov parallelohedra up to
  combinatorial equivalence.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Parallelohedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/parallelohedron)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Grünbaum, B., *The Bilinski dodecahedron and assorted parallelohedra, zonohedra, monohedra,
  isozonohedra, and otherhedra*, Math. Intelligencer 32 (2010), 5–15](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00283-010-9138-7)
-/

namespace CanEverySphericalNonConvexPolyhedronThatTilesSpaceByTranslationHaveI

open Topology

local notation "ℝ³" => Fin 3 → ℝ

/-- An affine subspace of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a *plane* if its direction has dimension $2$. -/
def IsPlane (H : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³) : Prop :=
  Module.finrank ℝ H.direction = 2

/-- A (solid) *spherical polyhedron* in $\mathbb{R}^3$: a compact set with nonempty interior
whose boundary is contained in finitely many planes and is homeomorphic to the $2$-sphere.
Convexity is not assumed. -/
structure IsSphericalPolyhedron (P : Set ℝ³) : Prop where
  isCompact : IsCompact P
  interior_nonempty : (interior P).Nonempty
  frontier_subset_planes : ∃ planes : Finset (AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³),
    (∀ H ∈ planes, IsPlane H) ∧ frontier P ⊆ ⋃ H ∈ planes, (H : Set ℝ³)
  frontier_homeomorph_sphere :
    Nonempty (frontier P ≃ₜ Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) 1)

/-- The *flat points* of the boundary of `P`: the boundary points near which the boundary
coincides with a plane. These are the points in the relative interiors of the faces. -/
def flatPoints (P : Set ℝ³) : Set ℝ³ :=
  {x ∈ frontier P | ∃ H : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³, IsPlane H ∧ ∃ U ∈ 𝓝 x, U ∩ frontier P = U ∩ H}

/-- The *faces* of `P`: the closures of the connected components of the set of flat boundary
points. Adjacent coplanar pieces of the boundary belong to the same face, so for a convex polytope
the faces are exactly its two-dimensional faces. -/
def faces (P : Set ℝ³) : Set (Set ℝ³) :=
  {F | ∃ x ∈ flatPoints P, F = closure (connectedComponentIn (flatPoints P) x)}

/-- `𝒢` is a *patch decomposition* of `P`: the members of `𝒢` are groups of faces of `P` with
connected union (the *patches*), and every face of `P` lies in exactly one group. -/
def IsPatchDecomposition (P : Set ℝ³) (𝒢 : Set (Set (Set ℝ³))) : Prop :=
  (∀ G ∈ 𝒢, G ⊆ faces P ∧ IsConnected (⋃₀ G)) ∧ ∀ F ∈ faces P, ∃! G ∈ 𝒢, F ∈ G

/-- The image of a set `A ⊆ ℝ³` under a homeomorphism `h : frontier P ≃ₜ frontier Q`, i.e. the
image under `h` of the part of `A` lying on the boundary of `P`. -/
def frontierImage {P Q : Set ℝ³} (h : frontier P ≃ₜ frontier Q) (A : Set ℝ³) : Set ℝ³ :=
  Subtype.val '' (h '' (Subtype.val ⁻¹' A))

/-- A family `𝒜` of subsets of the boundary of `P` and a family `ℬ` of subsets of the boundary
of `Q` have the *same combinatorial structure* if some homeomorphism `frontier P ≃ₜ frontier Q`
maps the members of `𝒜` exactly onto the members of `ℬ`. When `𝒜` and `ℬ` are the cells of
cell decompositions of the two boundary spheres, this says that the two cell complexes are
combinatorially equivalent. -/
def HaveSameCombinatorialStructure (P Q : Set ℝ³) (𝒜 ℬ : Set (Set ℝ³)) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : frontier P ≃ₜ frontier Q, ∀ B, B ∈ ℬ ↔ ∃ A ∈ 𝒜, frontierImage h A = B

/-- A *parallelohedron* is a convex polyhedron that tiles space by translation. By the theorems
of Fedorov and Venkov–McMullen, every parallelohedron is combinatorially equivalent to one of the
five Fedorov parallelohedra: the parallelepiped, the hexagonal prism, the rhombic dodecahedron,
the elongated dodecahedron and the truncated octahedron. -/
def IsParallelohedron (Q : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsSphericalPolyhedron Q ∧ Convex ℝ Q ∧ tilesByTranslation Q

/-- Every face of `P` is a subset of the boundary of `P`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem subset_frontier_of_mem_faces {P F : Set ℝ³} (hF : F ∈ faces P) : F ⊆ frontier P := by
  obtain ⟨x, -, rfl⟩ := hF
  refine (closure_mono ?_).trans isClosed_frontier.closure_eq.subset
  exact (connectedComponentIn_subset _ _).trans fun y hy ↦ hy.1

/-- Every face of `P` is connected. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem isConnected_of_mem_faces {P F : Set ℝ³} (hF : F ∈ faces P) : IsConnected F := by
  obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := hF
  exact (isConnected_connectedComponentIn_iff.mpr hx).closure

/-- Taking every face as its own patch is a patch decomposition. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem isPatchDecomposition_singleton (P : Set ℝ³) :
    IsPatchDecomposition P ((fun F ↦ {F}) '' faces P) := by
  refine ⟨?_, fun F hF ↦ ⟨{F}, ⟨⟨F, hF, rfl⟩, rfl⟩, ?_⟩⟩
  · rintro G ⟨F, hF, rfl⟩
    simpa using ⟨hF, isConnected_of_mem_faces hF⟩
  · rintro G ⟨⟨F', -, rfl⟩, hF'⟩
    simpa using hF'.symm

/-- The trivial patch decomposition of `P` has the same combinatorial structure as the faces
of `P`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem haveSameCombinatorialStructure_self (P : Set ℝ³) :
    HaveSameCombinatorialStructure P P (Set.sUnion '' ((fun F ↦ {F}) '' faces P)) (faces P) := by
  have key : ∀ F ∈ faces P, frontierImage (Homeomorph.refl (frontier P)) F = F := by
    intro F hF
    simp only [frontierImage, Homeomorph.refl_apply, Set.image_id, Subtype.image_preimage_coe]
    exact Set.inter_eq_right.mpr (subset_frontier_of_mem_faces hF)
  refine ⟨Homeomorph.refl _, fun B ↦ ⟨fun hB ↦ ⟨B, ⟨{B}, ⟨B, hB, rfl⟩, Set.sUnion_singleton B⟩,
    key B hB⟩, ?_⟩⟩
  rintro ⟨A, ⟨G, ⟨F, hF, rfl⟩, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
  simpa [key F hF] using hF

/-- Every parallelohedron satisfies the conclusion of Grünbaum's conjecture (with itself as the
comparison parallelohedron), so the conjecture is only about non-convex polyhedra. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem IsParallelohedron.exists_patchDecomposition {P : Set ℝ³} (hP : IsParallelohedron P) :
    ∃ (Q : Set ℝ³) (𝒢 : Set (Set (Set ℝ³))), IsParallelohedron Q ∧ IsPatchDecomposition P 𝒢 ∧
      HaveSameCombinatorialStructure P Q (Set.sUnion '' 𝒢) (faces Q) :=
  ⟨P, _, hP, isPatchDecomposition_singleton P, haveSameCombinatorialStructure_self P⟩

/--
**Grünbaum's conjecture.** Can every spherical non-convex polyhedron that tiles space by
translation have its faces grouped into patches with the same combinatorial structure as a
parallelohedron?

That is: for every polyhedron $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ whose boundary is topologically a
sphere and whose translated copies tile space, do there exist a parallelohedron $Q$ (a convex
polyhedron that tiles space by translation, i.e. one of the five Fedorov parallelohedra) and a
grouping of the faces of $P$ into connected patches such that some homeomorphism from the boundary
of $P$ to the boundary of $Q$ maps the patches exactly onto the faces of $Q$?

The conjectured answer is yes. Convexity of $P$ is not assumed; the convex case holds trivially.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem can_every_spherical_non_convex_polyhedron_that_tiles_space_by_translation_have_i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ P : Set ℝ³, IsSphericalPolyhedron P → tilesByTranslation P →
      ∃ (Q : Set ℝ³) (𝒢 : Set (Set (Set ℝ³))), IsParallelohedron Q ∧ IsPatchDecomposition P 𝒢 ∧
        HaveSameCombinatorialStructure P Q (Set.sUnion '' 𝒢) (faces Q) := by
  sorry

end CanEverySphericalNonConvexPolyhedronThatTilesSpaceByTranslationHaveI

The notes' parenthetical that the article's tiling is face-to-face applies to the definition of parallelohedron; for the conjecture itself the source only says 'can tile space by translation', so no face-to-face condition was imposed on P (and none is needed for Q by Venkov–McMullen).
modeling_decisions: Space is `Fin 3 → ℝ` (local notation ℝ³) so that the repository's existing `tilesByTranslation` (defined on `Fin d → ℝ`) can be reused; topology is the same as the Euclidean one.

'Polyhedron that is topologically a sphere' is modelled as a solid: `IsSphericalPolyhedron P` = `IsCompact P`, `(interior P).Nonempty`, `frontier P` contained in finitely many planes (affine subspaces of direction-dimension 2), and `frontier P ≃ₜ` the unit 2-sphere. Convexity is NOT assumed. Nonempty interior is needed so that the tiling hypothesis is not vacuously satisfiable by a hollow surface; compactness plus the sphere boundary then force P to be the closed region bounded by the polyhedral sphere.

The hypothesis 'non-convex' from the list-page statement is not added as `¬ Convex ℝ P`, following the decomposition notes and the article's formulation of Grünbaum's conjecture ('for every polyhedron that is topologically a sphere and can tile space by translation'); the convex case is trivially true (proved in the file as the `category test` theorem `IsParallelohedron.exists_patchDecomposition`), so both readings are equivalent.

'Tiles space by translation' uses the existing `tilesByTranslation` (countable translation set, translates cover up to measure zero and overlap in measure zero). For a compact set with nonempty interior and null boundary (as here) this is equivalent to an exact tiling with pairwise disjoint interiors. No face-to-face condition is imposed on the tiling of P (the source says only 'tile space by translation'); this is the weaker hypothesis, hence the stronger conjecture, and includes translational tiles that only tile in a staggered way.

Faces are defined intrinsically (maximal-face convention): `flatPoints P` = boundary points near which the boundary coincides with a plane; `faces P` = closures of connected components of `flatPoints P`. Adjacent coplanar boundary pieces thus form one face, and a face may in principle be a polygon with holes (e.g. a face carrying a bump); for a convex polytope the faces are exactly its 2-dimensional faces. Because every face must lie in a single patch, this is the hardest (strongest) reading of 'group its faces'.

A patch decomposition is a partition `𝒢` of `faces P` into groups with connected union (`IsPatchDecomposition`); the patches are `Set.sUnion '' 𝒢`. Connectedness is redundant given the conclusion but is kept because the source says 'unions of connected subsets of faces'.

    (Metric.sphere (0 : E3) 1 ≃ₜ (frontier carrier : Set E3))

a nonempty collection of those pseudo-faces. -/
def IsFaceCell {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → Set E3) (c : Set E3) : Prop :=
  c.Nonempty ∧ ∃ I : Set (Fin n), I.Nonempty ∧ c = ⋂ i ∈ I, f i

/-- The incidence poset generated by a finite family of closed pseudo-faces: its elements are
all nonempty intersections of nonempty collections of pseudo-faces, ordered by inclusion. -/

  {c : Set E3 // IsFaceCell f c}

intersection of two distinct tiles is a face, edge, or vertex of each translated face complex. -/

          ((v +ᵥ P.carrier) ∩ (w +ᵥ P.carrier)))

- [Parallelohedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/parallelohedron)
-/

namespace CanEverySphericalNonConvexPolyhedronThatTilesSpaceByTranslationHaveI

open Set

local notation "ℝ³" => Fin 3 → ℝ

/-- The translate of `s` by the vector `t`. -/
def translate (s : Set ℝ³) (t : ℝ³) : Set ℝ³ :=
  {x | x - t ∈ s}

/-- A polygon is a two-dimensional convex hull of finitely many points. -/
def IsPolygon (s : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ v : Finset ℝ³, s = convexHull ℝ (v : Set ℝ³) ∧
    Module.finrank ℝ (vectorSpan ℝ s) = 2

/-- A polyhedron is represented by its solid body and its finite collection of polygonal
facets. Its boundary is required to be exactly the union of the facets and to be a topological
2-sphere. Convexity is not required. -/
structure Polyhedron where
  body : Set ℝ³
  faces : Finset (Set ℝ³)
  compact_body : IsCompact body
  interior_nonempty : (interior body).Nonempty
  frontier_eq_iUnion_faces : frontier body = ⋃ f ∈ faces, f
  polygonal_faces : ∀ f ∈ faces, IsPolygon f
  face_intersections : ∀ f ∈ faces, ∀ g ∈ faces, f ≠ g →
    f ∩ g ⊆ intrinsicFrontier ℝ f ∩ intrinsicFrontier ℝ g
  maximal_faces : ∀ f ∈ faces, ∀ s : Set ℝ³,
    IsPolygon s → f ⊆ s → s ⊆ frontier body → s = f
  spherical : Nonempty (frontier body ≃ₜ Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1)

/-- A face cell is the empty face or the intersection of the body with a collection of its
facets. This includes the body, facets, edges, and vertices. -/
def Polyhedron.IsFaceCell (P : Polyhedron) (c : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  c = ∅ ∨ ∃ fs : Set (Set ℝ³), fs ⊆ (P.faces : Set (Set ℝ³)) ∧
    c = P.body ∩ ⋂₀ fs

/-- The translated copies indexed by `T` form a locally finite, face-to-face tiling of space.
Exact coverage and disjoint interiors express that the copies are tiles; the final condition
says that every intersection of two copies is a face cell of each copy. -/
def IsFaceToFaceTranslationalTiling (P : Polyhedron) (T : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  (⋃ t ∈ T, translate P.body t) = univ ∧
  T.PairwiseDisjoint (fun t ↦ interior (translate P.body t)) ∧
  LocallyFinite (fun t : T ↦ translate P.body t) ∧
  ∀ t ∈ T, ∀ u ∈ T,
    ∃ c d : Set ℝ³, P.IsFaceCell c ∧ P.IsFaceCell d ∧
      translate P.body t ∩ translate P.body u = translate c t ∧
      translate P.body t ∩ translate P.body u = translate d u

/-- A polyhedron tiles face-to-face by translations. -/
def IsFaceToFaceTranslationalTile (P : Polyhedron) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set ℝ³, IsFaceToFaceTranslationalTiling P T

/-- A parallelohedron is a convex polyhedron that tiles space face-to-face by translations. -/
def IsParallelohedron (P : Polyhedron) : Prop :=
  Convex ℝ P.body ∧ IsFaceToFaceTranslationalTile P

/-- The facets of `P` can be grouped into connected patches with the combinatorial structure of
the facets of `Q` if a surjection assigns source facets to target facets and a homeomorphism of
the two boundaries carries each resulting patch onto its assigned target facet. Thus patch
boundaries, their intersections (pseudo-edges), and their vertices are all preserved. -/
def HasPatchStructureOf (P Q : Polyhedron) : Prop :=
  ∃ (g : P.faces → Q.faces) (h : frontier P.body ≃ₜ frontier Q.body),
    Function.Surjective g ∧
    ∀ q : Q.faces,
      let patch : Set ℝ³ := {x | ∃ f : P.faces, g f = q ∧ x ∈ (f : Set ℝ³)}
      IsConnected patch ∧
        (fun x : frontier P.body ↦ ((h x : frontier Q.body) : ℝ³)) ''
          {x : frontier P.body | (x : ℝ³) ∈ patch} = (q : Set ℝ³)

/-- **Grünbaum's conjecture.** Does every polyhedron in `ℝ³` whose boundary is topologically a
sphere and whose translated copies form a face-to-face tiling of space have its faces grouped
into connected patches with the same combinatorial structure as the faces of a parallelohedron
(equivalently, one of the five Fedorov parallelohedra)? Convexity is not assumed. -/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem can_every_spherical_non_convex_polyhedron_that_tiles_space_by_translation_have_i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ P : Polyhedron, IsFaceToFaceTranslationalTile P →
      ∃ Q : Polyhedron, IsParallelohedron Q ∧ HasPatchStructureOf P Q := by
  sorry

end CanEverySphericalNonConvexPolyhedronThatTilesSpaceByTranslationHaveI
modeling_decisions: Following the background article and the fixed decomposition notes, “non-convex” is treated as emphasizing the previously unknown cases, not as a hypothesis excluding convex polyhedra: the theorem quantifies over all polyhedra whose boundary is a sphere, without assuming convexity.

A polyhedron is modeled as a compact solid with nonempty interior and finitely many maximal polygonal facets whose union is its frontier. The frontier is required to be homeomorphic to the unit 2-sphere. Distinct facets may meet only along their intrinsic frontiers.

“Tiles space by translation” is read as a locally finite face-to-face tiling: translates cover all of ℝ³ exactly, have pairwise disjoint interiors, and every intersection of two translated tiles is a translated face cell of each tile.

A face cell is the empty face or an intersection of the body with a collection of facets, so this includes the body, facets, edges, and vertices and allows the face-to-face condition to cover all tile intersections.

Rather than hard-coding the five Fedorov incidence tables, a parallelohedron is defined intrinsically as a convex polyhedron admitting a face-to-face translational tiling. In dimension three these are exactly the five Fedorov combinatorial types cited by the source.

“Same combinatorial structure” is modeled by a cellular homeomorphism between the two spherical boundaries that carries every connected union of source facets in a fiber of the grouping map exactly onto its target parallelohedron facet. This preserves patch facets, pseudo-edges, vertices, and all incidences, rather than only the facet adjacency graph.
